title: Redesign early-PR landing note so the gate accepts it and numbers fit
summary: Retry of rejected job 20261109-201651-ggxj: write docs/design/early-pr-no-staging-branch.md (early per-job PR, no staging branch) plus a CHANGELOG.md entry. The note fixes each prior verifier finding: a commit order the landing gate accepts, a saving bounded by measured stage data, and consistent citation duties. Audience: Athena maintainers and the next throughput review.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the note's commit order and saving arithmetic against cited sources, not mere section existence.
Every figure in the note cites its source and is labeled measured, sample, or predicted.
The note includes an Existing code section and alternatives considered.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal and audience: a design note that Athena maintainers can build from and the next throughput review can score; the request is to design the change, not implement it.

Prior job 20261109-201651-ggxj (rejected, verdict fail): its candidate changed CHANGELOG.md and added docs/design/early-pr-no-staging-branch.md. Both are kept as deliverables, but the work is redone from the base, since the candidate is discarded. Each of its five findings is a criterion below (commit order vs gate, 7.0 vs 3.7 minute bound, re-measurement, CHANGELOG criterion, citation duty).

Existing code: docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md, docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, docs/design/per-job-landing-branches.md, docs/design/continuous-landing.md and docs/design/records-history.md exist in the snapshot; the note reuses or extends them in an Existing code section stating what is kept, changed or superseded.

THROUGHPUT.md and the throughput review 20261109-201520-z1xg are not in the snapshot (no THROUGHPUT.md found by glob). The note cites them as the request's quoted source and labels any figure it cannot re-read as quoted, not re-measured; the 1859.9 and 1811.5 figures are quoted from the request and measured by the review.

Environment: the note discusses GitHub pull requests and CI on the host repository; the producer reads and writes only repository files and reaches no network, CI, or records branch. Read-only repository docs are the only data used.

Existing evidence for the gate rule: docs/design/records-history.md and docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md describe that a landing commit adds the verifier's closing records (candidate.json, verification.json, outcome-landed.json); the producer must read these before writing section 2.

The saving figure: the review predicted 7.0 minutes per landed job; the prior verifier's measured split gives checks 1.0 and verifier 2.7 minutes, so overlap bounds the saving near 3.7 minutes. The note keeps 7.0 as the review's prediction to be scored and states the gap, or names the other mechanism with its source.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/early-pr-no-staging-branch.md exists (created) and describes opening each job's PR when the producer finishes, building the landing commit on the host's current main, and dropping the local staging branch.

Section 2 of the note gives the exact order of commits: what is built at producer end, what the verifier adds, what is pushed, what CI sees, which commit lands, and when a rebuild or force-push is needed. It states that the landing commit must contain the verifier's closing records (candidate.json, verification.json, outcome-landed.json) citing docs/design/records-history.md and docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md, and it does not claim the verifier runs against the same commit that lands unless it explains how CI results carry over (for example reuse keyed on tree) or the records move to the athena/records branch.
The force-push/rebuild section of the note is consistent with that commit order, checkable by reading both sections in the file.

The saving section recomputes the saving from stage durations (checks 1.0 and verifier 2.7 minutes, plus the cited per-job-main-landing.md figures), states each figure's source and whether it is measured or sample, says overlap can save at most about 3.7 minutes, keeps 7.0 minutes per landed job against the 1859.9-minute median as the review's labeled prediction, and states the gap or names the other mechanism.

The note states how the next throughput review measures the minutes after the change lands, cites throughput review 20261109-201520-z1xg, states that a change implementing it must cite that review in its request text, and says how this duty relates to the review 20261109-014617-5cg0 duty in docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md when one change implements both.

The note has an Existing code section reusing or extending docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md, docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, docs/design/per-job-landing-branches.md and docs/design/continuous-landing.md, saying what is kept, changed or superseded, and lists alternatives considered.

CHANGELOG.md has a new entry for the note. git diff shows only docs/design/early-pr-no-staging-branch.md and CHANGELOG.md changed, with no changes to crates/, xtask/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
Run cargo test and cargo clippy: both pass, so the policy tests accept the new note and changelog.

out_of_scope: Implementing the change in crates/ or xtask/
Editing existing design notes beyond optional cross-links
departures: Slightly lower verification pass chance: this is the second retry of a design with substantive soundness findings.
